avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may increase fluticasone metabolism and reduce systemic exposure/efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative herbal supplements

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice Root
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Mineralocorticoid effects may potentiate corticosteroid-induced hypertension and hypokalemia
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use only under medical supervision with electrolyte monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Echinacea
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have immunostimulant properties that could counteract immunosuppressive effects of corticosteroids
caution_supplements.action: Use cautiously; monitor for reduced therapeutic effect

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 modulation; may affect fluticasone metabolism variably
caution_supplements.action: Monitor clinical response; coordinate with healthcare provider if using

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May potentiate corticosteroid-induced fluid retention and hypertension
caution_foods.action: Limit sodium intake; maintain dietary balance

caution_foods.name: Foods high in simple sugars
caution_foods.mechanism: Corticosteroids can impair glucose tolerance; high sugar intake may worsen hyperglycemia risk

monitoring_notes: Fluticasone is primarily metabolized via CYP3A4 and undergoes extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism, resulting in low systemic bioavailability with inhaled/intranasal use. Monitor for signs of adrenal suppression with long-term use, particularly with concurrent CYP3A4 inhibitors, and counsel on proper inhalation technique to maximize local benefit while minimizing systemic exposure.
